memo: Base: the pipeline embedded in sanpier (Saner Turhaner) 'Candidate-aware PubChem promotion 0.465' (frozen_0465.ipynb) = dmitriigluzdov 'CASMI 26: The Data Behind Spectra to Structures' v16 (public 0.464) + sanpier's candidate-specific rank-1 PubChem promotion (public 0.465), kernels/e3/base_f465.ipynb, unchanged except the cells marked ours. Ours: own COCONUT table into engine 2's pool (ownco) and learned peak credits in the fragment scorer (lfrag) = e3f465oc-1, LB 0.467, our best. New here (port, not ours): sanpier's neural rerank of the final 25 from 'PubChem + Neural025 - LB 0.466' (his spectrum-candidate dual encoder, dataset sanpier/casmi-spectrum-model-v1; baseline rank + neural rank reciprocal-rank fusion, weight 0.25, offset 3; candidate set kept), modules copied unchanged into kernels/e3/nn_port (its frozen pipeline is byte-identical to our base). Question: does a learned spectrum-candidate score (the 'ranker' direction of our 10-24 plan) still add on top of our own two parts? Public effect on the plain base was 0.465 -> 0.466 (about one molecule's partial ranks), so this is below the 2-molecule bar alone; it is the first test of the learned-ranker signal and the input for tomorrow's bundle with the two-pipeline fusion. Hypothesis: LB >= 0.468. build.py f465nn base=f465 ownco=1 lfrag=1 nn=0.25.
